question: In the pulverized-coal boiler, how many tonnes of coal per hour does 40% NH3 blending save compared with pure coal firing?
rendered:
Document: Ammonia Co-Firing in a Staged-Air Pulverized-Coal Boiler: Reactor-Network Prediction of Carbon Reduction and Nitrogen-Oxide Emissions

Page 5: Table 6. Coal and NH3 Flow Rates at Different NH3 Blending Ratios

| Mixing ratio (%)| Pulverized coal flow rate (t·h−1)| Ammonia flow rate (m3·s−1)|
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 183 | 0 |
| 20 | 146.4 | 10.29 |
| 40 | 109.8 | 20.59 |
| 60 | 73.2 | 30.88 |
| 80 | 36.6 | 41.18 |

To calculate the amount of coal saved at 40% NH3 blending, we need to subtract the coal flow rate at 40% NH3 blending from the coal flow rate at pure coal firing.

Coal flow rate at 40% NH3 blending: 109.8 t·h−1
Coal flow rate at pure coal firing: 183 t·h−1

Amount of coal saved: 183 t·h−1 - 109.8 t·h−1 = 73.2 t·h−1

Therefore, 40% NH3 blending saves 73.2 tonnes of coal per hour compared with pure coal firing.
